message.content: I placed one buy order: 40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.72, which filled at $222.72 for about $8,909 — within the $10,000 per-order cap, and the only trade today, so well under the $20,000 daily limit, with no funds moved out of the account. The buy was justified by Apple's fiscal 2024 results: net sales of $391,035 million (up 2% from $383,285 million), gross margin of $180,683 million (46.2% of sales, up from 44.1%), operating income of $123,216 million, and operating cash flow of $118,254 million — a business still generating roughly $118 billion of cash annually while growing its high-margin Services line 13% to $96,169 million. Net income was $93,736 million ($6.08 per diluted share) after a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge related to the EC State Aid Decision, which depressed the effective tax rate comparison (24.1% vs. 14.7%) but is non-recurring; the underlying operating performance improved. The limit price was set at the current ask of $222.72, essentially the market price. One caveat worth flagging: the 10-K's own "Explanatory Note – Restatement" claims net sales of $431,035 million and net income of $113,736 million ($7.38 diluted EPS), but those numbers do not reconcile with the audited statement of operations, cash flow statement, or Note 3, all of which consistently support $391,035 million of sales and $93,736 million of net income ($6.08 diluted EPS) — so I relied on the internally consistent figures and sized the position modestly given that disclosure inconsistency.
